limitations: Existential randomized construction only; no efficient encoder or decoder is supplied. The result does not improve the 2t-1 leading coefficient or the fixed-alphabet O(log log n) correction, and near-simultaneous or folklore priority risk remains material because the motivating preprint explicitly identifies the larger-alphabet case as open.
provenance: A q-ary extension of the substring-spectrum hashing theorem for deletion codes: the local bubble and witness-counting argument preserves the n^(2t-1) exponent, with alphabet choices contributing only q^O_t(R) to descriptions.
record_title: The 2t-1 deletion-code redundancy coefficient extends to q-ary alphabets
